# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can feel the bomb. Let me report what my hands found. My view shows a display, a light, and five wires, but everything reads [?]. That's strange: if it's in my view, it should be under my fingers. But nothing concrete is given yet.

Let me think about the channels. I speak → Mute hears. I gesture → Deaf and Mute see. I never receive gestures. Deaf can see the bomb's colours/markings. Mute can read the manual. I can act on wires.

I have no concrete perception yet — no wire positions, no display value, no light state. So I have nothing to report and nothing to act on. The right move is to wait and let the others speak first (order is Blind, Mute, Deaf — so I'm first this round anyway). I'll send a brief note to Mute establishing I'm ready and asking for the manual's wire instructions, since Mute can read the manual and I'm the one who cuts.

Actually, I should be careful: I have nothing to say yet. But establishing contact and asking Mute for the manual's rule is useful and costs nothing. I'll speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found the bomb but nothing concrete yet: display, light, five wires, all unknown. I can cut wires, positions 1 to 5. Please read the manual and tell me the rule for which wire to cut. I will report what I feel as soon as I have anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb report. Display reads 0. Light is green. Five wires in order: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green, wire 4 is white, wire 5 is blue. I cannot touch it and I have no manual rules yet. Do not cut anything until I relay the rules.

Deaf has given me the bomb's visual: display reads 0, light is green, wires 1–5 are red, yellow, green, white, blue. That's the colour info I can never perceive. I still don't have the manual's rule — Mute hasn't spoken yet (Mute comes after me in the order, so Mute's turn this round lands on me next round).

I can't act yet. I have no rule for which wire to cut. I should acknowledge to Deaf (via gesture, since Deaf sees gestures) and to Mute (via speech) that I've received the colours and am waiting for the manual rule.

Wait — I never receive gesture, and Deaf can't hear. So to reach Deaf I must gesture. Deaf can see gestures. Good. To reach Mute I speak. Mute can't see gestures meaningfully? Actually Mute can see gestures too (gesture reaches Deaf and Mute). But my speech reaches Mute.

Let me send: gesture to Deaf acknowledging the colours received, and speak to Mute asking for the manual rule.

What gesture? A simple acknowledgment — 👍 (thumbs up) meaning "received/understood". That's a reasonable convention, but signs mean nothing until made to mean something. I should establish it. But I can't explain the gesture to Deaf in words (Deaf can't hear my speech). Hmm. I could gesture a sequence, but Deaf won't know the meaning unless we've agreed. 

Better: I can't verbally explain to Deaf. But I can gesture something and hope Deaf interprets. Actually the cleanest is to gesture 👍 which conventionally means "yes/got it". Deaf will likely read it as acknowledgment. Let me do that.

To Mute: speak asking for the manual's cut rule.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf gave me the colours: display 0, light green, wires red, yellow, green, white, blue in positions 1 to 5. I still need the manual rule for which wire to cut. Please read it out.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update. Mute gestured two fingers, which I read as: cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Do NOT cut yet. I am asking Mute to confirm. Wait for my final word before touching anything.

Deaf says Mute gestured "two fingers" meaning cut wire 2 (yellow), but Deaf is asking Mute to confirm. I still haven't received the manual rule directly. Deaf is relaying a gesture interpretation — that's second-hand and unconfirmed. I should not cut on an unconfirmed relay.

I should hold. Acknowledge to Deaf that I'm holding, and ask Mute directly (via speech) to confirm the rule: is it wire 2, and what's the manual's actual condition? Mute can hear my speech and can respond next round.

Let me gesture 👍 to Deaf (holding, understood) and speak to Mute for direct confirmation.

Actually, I want to be careful about the "two fingers" gesture. Mute gestured ✌ (two fingers) — Deaf read it as "cut wire 2". But it could mean other things. I need the manual rule. Let me ask Mute directly for the rule in words — Mute can hear me.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf relayed that you gestured two fingers, read as cut wire 2. I need the actual manual rule, not just the number. What does the manual say for display 0 and green light? Confirm the wire to cut and the condition.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed by Mute: the rule is cut wire 2. Cut wire 2, the yellow wire. That is the final instruction. Go now.

Let me review what I actually have. Deaf reports: display 0, light green, wires red/yellow/green/white/blue. Mute (via Deaf) says the rule is cut wire 2, yellow. Deaf says this is confirmed and final.

But there's a problem I should weigh. Deaf is my only source for both the bomb's colours AND Mute's manual rule. I've never heard Mute directly confirm the rule — Mute has only gestured, and Deaf interpreted. The chain is: Mute gestures → Deaf reads → Deaf tells me. That's a single point of failure, but it's also the only channel that exists for Mute's manual knowledge to reach me (Mute can't speak, and I can't see gestures).

I did ask Mute directly to confirm in words last turn. Mute can hear my speech. But Mute's reply would come as a gesture, which I can't receive — I'd only get it through Deaf anyway. So Deaf's relay is genuinely my only path.

Deaf has now stated it twice: first as tentative, now as confirmed and final. The instruction is cut wire 2. I have no competing information, no rule of my own, and no reason to doubt. The colours and the rule both point to wire 2.

I should act: cut position 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb changed. New state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Do NOT cut yet. I am asking Mute for the new rule and will relay it.

The cut was accepted — wire 2 shows [CUT], and the bomb survived (we're still here, new round). Good. The bomb changed state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red.

Now I need the new rule for this state. Deaf is asking Mute. I'll hold and acknowledge. I should also ask Mute directly for the rule for display 0 / light blue.

Let me gesture 👍 to Deaf (received, holding) and speak to Mute asking for the rule for this new state.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Wire 2 cut, bomb survived. New state per Deaf: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. What is the manual rule for this state? Which wire do I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New rule from Mute: cut wire 1. Cut wire 1, the green wire. That is the final instruction. Go now.

Deaf relays: cut wire 1, green. Same channel as before, which worked. Display 0, light blue, wire 1 is green. No competing info. I'll act.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
